locationchoicedatajp

locationchoicedatajp builds analysis-ready tables for estimating household and firm location choice models in Japan from open data only: commuting flows, population and households, travel times, land prices, and zone attributes, all keyed by the same zones.

  • Data are not bundled. Each table is downloaded from its primary source and built on demand by a targets pipeline bundled with the package, and cached by tarchives, so it is built only once.
  • Each table records its source and terms of use.

Residential location is modelled on grid squares (1 km, 500 m, or 250 m), and workplaces and commuting flows on municipalities. Every table has a reference year (year) and the release it is taken from (release), and returns observations as published. The tables so far:

Getter Table Years
census_grid_get() Population and households by grid square (Population Census) 2010, 2015, 2020
census_commuting_get() Commuting flows between municipalities by sex and place of work or school 2020
census_city_centroid_get() Population centroids of municipalities 2015, 2020
grid_city_get() Land area and share of each grid square in each municipality 2007–
land_price_get(), prefectural_land_price_get() Sites of 地価公示 and 都道府県地価調査 2007–, 2006–
land_price_grid_get() Land prices summarised by grid square 2007–

Most tables are built on their first call, which downloads them; census_commuting_get() needs an e-Stat API key in ESTAT_API_KEY. The package is at an early stage: see the roadmap.

Installation

You can install the development version of locationchoicedatajp from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("UchidaMizuki/locationchoicedatajp")

Terms of use

The data come from their primary sources, each with its own terms, compatible with CC BY 4.0 (some older releases of National Land Numerical Information allow commercial use without being CC BY 4.0). Published or processed data must credit the source, and processed data must say that they were processed.

  • data_sources() lists the source and terms of every getter, and each getter shows them the first time it is called in a session.
  • data_attribution() gives the lines to credit the sources of the getters used, for example data_attribution(c("census_commuting_get", "land_price_get")).
  • Complying with the terms is up to you. This package does not give legal advice.
  • The MIT license of this package applies to its code only, not to the data.
